candidate_summary: Statistics student | SQL + Python | Kaggle enthusiast Recent: Data Intern (part-time) at Food Delivery Startup (fictional). Skills: SQL, Python, pandas, Power BI, Excel, scikit-learn (basic).

questions.question: To start, tell me about a finding from your own data work that changed what someone actually did.
questions.rationale: The team's analyses must lead to decisions by ops managers.

questions.question: Walk me through a SQL query you're proud of, for example one using joins or window functions.
questions.rationale: Joins, aggregations and window functions are named in the must-have.

questions.question: How would you design an A/B test to check whether a new rider bonus reduces evening delivery times?
questions.rationale: The intern helps design and read A/B tests on Dune Mobility's own metrics.

questions.question: Tell me about a dataset you cleaned in Python or R. What did you do about missing or messy values?
questions.rationale: Checks pandas-style cleaning and attention to detail with real data.

questions.question: Tell me about a time a number in your data looked wrong. How did you dig into why?
questions.rationale: Curiosity about why numbers look the way they do is a stated soft skill.

questions.question: Delivery times are often skewed by a few very late orders. How would you summarise them for an ops manager?
questions.rationale: Directly tests averages versus medians and distributions on the team's own kind of data.

questions.question: Finally, what makes you want to analyse ride-hailing and delivery data at Dune Mobility?
questions.rationale: Closes with motivation for the domain and the six-month internship.
